# HeartRateLab Evaluation Pipeline in Action

This notebook demonstrates the complete evaluation pipeline implemented in HeartRateLab.jl:
- **Mode 1**: Continuous feature extraction
- **Mode 2**: Windowed feature analysis
- **Mode 3**: Synthetic ensemble generation and comparison
- **Comparison**: Statistical distribution testing

## Setup

```{julia}
using HeartRateLab
using DataFrames, Random, Statistics, Plots
using Plots: histogram, plot!

# Set random seed for reproducibility
Random.seed!(42)

println("✓ Packages loaded successfully")
println("✓ Working directory: $(pwd())")
```

## Part 1: Load Real Data

```{julia}
# Load example HRV data
data_path = "test/testdata/example.txt"
real_ibis = read_txt(data_path)

println("✓ Loaded $(length(real_ibis)) IBI samples")
println("  Range: $(minimum(real_ibis))—$(maximum(real_ibis)) ms")
println("  Mean: $(round(mean(real_ibis); digits=1)) ms")
println("  Std: $(round(std(real_ibis); digits=1)) ms")
```

## Part 2: MODE 1 - Continuous Feature Extraction

Extract all 44 HRV features from the complete timeseries:

```{julia}
# Extract features from full dataset
real_features_dict = extract_feature_set(real_ibis)

println("✓ Extracted $(length(real_features_dict)) features")
println("\nSample features:")
sample_features = [:mean, :std_ibi, :rmssd, :pnn50, :lf_hf_ratio, :sd1, :sd2]
for feat in sample_features
    if haskey(real_features_dict, feat)
        val = real_features_dict[feat]
        println("  $feat: $(round(val; digits=2))")
    end
end
```

## Part 3: MODE 2 - Windowed Analysis

Split the continuous timeseries into overlapping windows and extract features from each:

```{julia}
# Windowed analysis: 300-beat windows with 50% overlap
window_size = 300
overlap = 150

windowed_real = windowed_feature_set(real_ibis; window_size=window_size, overlap=overlap)

println("✓ Windowed analysis complete")
println("  Window size: $window_size beats (~4-5 minutes)")
println("  Overlap: $overlap beats (50%)")
println("  Number of windows: $(nrow(windowed_real))")
println("  Features per window: $(ncol(windowed_real))")
println("\nFirst window statistics:")
println("  Mean IBI: $(round(mean(windowed_real.mean[1]); digits=1)) ms")
println("  RMSSD: $(round(windowed_real.rmssd[1]; digits=1)) ms")
```

## Part 4: MODE 3 - Synthetic Ensemble Generation

Fit a model to the data, then generate synthetic ensemble:

```{julia}
println("Fitting LIF model to data...")
lif_model = LIF(; τ=50.0, I_base=0.5, threshold=1.0, noise_amp=0.1)

# Use a small subset for faster fitting (demo purposes)
demo_data = real_ibis[1:500]  # Use first 500 beats
result = fit(lif_model, demo_data; method=:gradient, max_iter=200)

println("✓ Model fitted successfully")
println("  Converged: $(result.diagnostics["converged"])")
println("  Final loss: $(round(result.diagnostics["loss_final"]; digits=4))")
println("  Parameters: $(result.params)")
```

## Part 5: Generate and Compare Ensembles

```{julia}
# Generate synthetic ensemble
println("Generating synthetic ensemble...")
ensemble_size = 100
ensemble = simulate_ensemble(lif_model, result.params, length(demo_data); n_sim=ensemble_size)

println("✓ Generated ensemble of $ensemble_size synthetic series")
println("  Each series: $(length(ensemble[1])) beats")
println("  Series 1 range: $(round(minimum(ensemble[1]); digits=0))—$(round(maximum(ensemble[1]); digits=0)) ms")
```

## Part 6: Extract Features from Ensemble

```{julia}
# Extract features from entire ensemble
println("Extracting features from ensemble...")
ensemble_features = extract_ensemble_features(ensemble)

println("✓ Extracted features from ensemble")
println("  Ensemble feature matrix size: $(size(ensemble_features))")
println("  Features: $(ncol(ensemble_features))")

# Show summary statistics
println("\nEnsemble feature summary (from synthetic data):")
println("  Mean IBI: μ=$(round(mean(ensemble_features.mean); digits=1))±$(round(std(ensemble_features.mean); digits=1)) ms")
println("  RMSSD: μ=$(round(mean(ensemble_features.rmssd); digits=1))±$(round(std(ensemble_features.rmssd); digits=1)) ms")
println("  LF/HF: μ=$(round(mean(ensemble_features.lf_hf_ratio); digits=2))±$(round(std(ensemble_features.lf_hf_ratio); digits=2))")
```

## Part 7: Statistical Comparison (eval_distributional)

Compare real data distribution to synthetic ensemble using statistical tests:

```{julia}
# Create real feature DataFrame (single observation)
real_df = DataFrame([Dict(k => v for (k, v) in pairs(real_features_dict))])

# Limit to features present in both
common_features = intersect(names(real_df), names(ensemble_features))

# Statistical comparison using Kolmogorov-Smirnov test
println("Running statistical tests (Kolmogorov-Smirnov)...")
comparison_results = eval_distributional(
    real_df[:, common_features],
    ensemble_features[:, common_features];
    test=:ks
)

println("\n✓ Statistical comparison complete")
println("  Total features tested: $(nrow(comparison_results))")
println("\nTop features (most different from ensemble):")
sort!(comparison_results, :p_value)
for i in 1:min(5, nrow(comparison_results))
    row = comparison_results[i, :]
    println("  $(row.feature): p=$(round(row.p_value; digits=4)), stat=$(round(row.statistic; digits=4))")
end
```

## Part 8: Visualization

Visualize the quality of model fit:

```{julia}
# Compare distributions of selected features
features_to_plot = [:mean, :rmssd, :sd1]

p = plot(layout=(1, 3), size=(1000, 300), legend=false)

for (idx, feat) in enumerate(features_to_plot)
    if feat in names(ensemble_features)
        # Get values
        real_val = real_df[1, feat]
        ensemble_vals = ensemble_features[!, feat]
        ensemble_vals = filter(!isnan, ensemble_vals)

        # Plot ensemble distribution
        histogram!(p[idx], ensemble_vals; alpha=0.6, bins=20, label="Ensemble", color=:blue)

        # Add real data as vertical line
        if !isnan(real_val)
            vline!(p[idx], [real_val]; color=:red, linewidth=2, label="Real")
        end

        title!(p[idx], string(feat))
        xlabel!(p[idx], "Value")
        ylabel!(p[idx], "Frequency")
    end
end

plot!(p, size=(1000, 300))
```

## Part 9: Summary and Interpretation

```{julia}
println("""
╔════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════╗
║                    EVALUATION PIPELINE SUMMARY                        ║
╚════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════╝

✓ MODE 1 (Continuous):
  - Extracted 44 HRV features from complete timeseries
  - Single feature vector per subject

✓ MODE 2 (Windowed):
  - Split timeseries into $(nrow(windowed_real)) overlapping windows
  - Feature distribution per window
  - Enables temporal analysis

✓ MODE 3 (Ensemble):
  - Fitted mechanistic model (LIF) to data
  - Generated $(ensemble_size) independent synthetic series
  - Extracted features from ensemble

✓ STATISTICAL COMPARISON:
  - Tested whether model reproduces real data statistics
  - Kolmogorov-Smirnov test: compares empirical CDFs
  - $(sum(comparison_results.p_value .< 0.05)) features significantly different (p<0.05)
  - $(sum(comparison_results.p_value .>= 0.05)) features match ensemble distribution

═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

This demonstrates the complete evaluation pipeline:

Real Data → Fit Model → Generate Ensemble → Extract Features → Compare

The pipeline is data-agnostic:
  • Synthetic data (from models) uses same feature extraction as real data
  • Comparison functions work with any feature distribution
  • Enables unified model validation across data modes

  - Add dataset infrastructure for PhysioNet benchmarking
  - Create visualization functions for publication-quality plots
""")
```

## Conclusion

The HeartRateLab evaluation pipeline successfully demonstrates:

1. **Complete data pipeline**: Load → Extract → Fit → Simulate → Evaluate
2. **Flexible analysis modes**: Continuous, windowed, and ensemble analysis
3. **Statistical rigor**: Formal hypothesis testing for model validation
4. **Unified comparison**: Model outputs treated identically to real data

The foundation is ready for advanced model validation and benchmarking against public datasets.
